advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify (with an offline test) that the shared-prefix breakpoint still lands at the prefix boundary under agentic cache settings (anthropic_cache / bedrock_cache_messages), or gate cache_prefix to single_turn calls only.
evidence: passes.py:333 `execution_mode="agentic" if agentic else "single_turn"` with `cache_prefix=prompts.shared_plan_prefix(plan)` set unconditionally at passes.py:322

capabilities.py:608 `_MESSAGE_TAIL_EXECUTION_MODES = frozenset({"agentic"})` and capabilities.py:654-655 `if cache_message_tail: anthropic_settings["anthropic_cache"] = True` (docstring line 631-633: automatic caching sends a TOP-LEVEL cache_control so 'the server places the breakpoint at the end of the prompt')

test_cache_prefix_breakpoint.py `_anthropic_settings`/`_bedrock_settings` both call `cache_settings_for(caps, execution_mode="single_turn")` — the agentic-mode (anthropic_cache / bedrock_cache_messages) path's breakpoint placement is never asserted
advisory.finding: The Pass-1 finder sets cache_prefix even when running execution_mode='agentic' (code-grounding tier), but in agentic mode cache_settings_for adds anthropic_cache=True / bedrock_cache_messages=True (a top-level / message-tail breakpoint at the END of the prompt). The breakpoint-relocation is only verified offline for single_turn settings, so the 'finder WRITE is READ by the verifier' guarantee is unproven — and may not hold — for the agentic finder path where the extra automatic-cache breakpoint changes the caching shape.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope the write-every-call-never-read diagnostic to a single run's rows (or document/justify that summarize's file-wide input is the intended aggregation).
evidence: usage_log.py:487 `warn_if_cache_write_never_read(rows, model=str(rows[0].get("model", "?")))` where `rows = _read(path)` is the whole file
usage_log.py:1-13 docstring: 'Process-level token-usage sink ... appends one JSON object per LLM call (JSONL)' — the sink is per-process, not per-run
structured_run.py:541 docstring 'True when a RUN's caching calls all WROTE the cache and NONE ever READ it' — scope mismatch with the file-wide caller
advisory.finding: warn_if_cache_write_never_read is invoked in usage_log.summarize over the ENTIRE JSONL sink, which is a process-level file that can span multiple runs, tickets, and models (per usage_log module docstring), yet cache_write_never_read is documented and reasoned as operating over 'a RUN's caching calls'. Across a multi-run file, one run's cache read clears the flag and masks another run's write-every-call-never-read pathology, and the WARNING labels everything with rows[0]['model'] even when rows mix models.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that drives the marked-prefix selection at runner.py:533-539 (or the extracted helper) asserting it returns cache_prefix when it is a proper prefix and the full system prompt otherwise.
evidence: runner.py:533-539 introduces `system_prompt=(req.cache_prefix if req.cache_prefix and req.system_prompt.startswith(req.cache_prefix) and len(req.cache_prefix) < len(req.system_prompt) else req.system_prompt)`

ABSENCE: `search_files(tests, "marked_prefix")` returns only test_cache_floor_per_model.py, which calls warn_if_cache_ineffective/estimate_marked_prefix_tokens directly with hand-built values and never drives runner.run() with a RunRequest carrying cache_prefix — so the new selection logic is unexercised.

test_cache_prefix_breakpoint.py pins only build_agent_kwargs and the telemetry helpers, not the runner's marked-span selection (grep of the file shows no estimate_marked_prefix_tokens / warn_if_cache_ineffective usage).
advisory.finding: The new runner branch that chooses req.cache_prefix (vs the full system prompt) as the marked-prefix span fed to estimate_marked_prefix_tokens has no test; a regression in that guard would silently mis-size cache-effectiveness telemetry (spurious warn or spurious silence) when a breakpoint has been relocated.
scenarios: A future edit inverts or drops the proper-prefix guard so the whole (large) system prompt is always measured, defeating the bug-e3cd correct-span fix for relocated breakpoints — no test turns red.
advisory.suggested_fix: Extract the ternary into a small pure helper (e.g. _marked_prefix_source(req) -> str) and unit-test it with (proper-prefix, non-prefix, None, equal-length) cases; or assert estimate_marked_prefix_tokens' input via a spy in a runner-level test.

evidence: runs.py:325-333 adds `shared_prefix = ctx.inputs.get("shared_prefix")` and computes cache_prefix from a proper-prefix guard, passed to RunRequest at runs.py:344 `cache_prefix=cache_prefix`.

test_execution_mode.py:83-135 — the three build_agent_request tests construct `_Ctx({...})` with no `inputs` carrying shared_prefix and assert only execution_mode/mode/output_schema; none assert req.cache_prefix.
ABSENCE: `search_files(tests, "cache_prefix")` returns only test_cache_prefix_breakpoint.py (agent_call/RunRequest level) — no hit in any build_agent_request/runs.py test.
advisory.finding: The new cache_prefix derivation in build_agent_request (runs.py) is untested: none of the three existing build_agent_request tests supply a `shared_prefix` input, so neither the set-when-proper-prefix branch nor the None fallback is exercised.
scenarios: A change to the proper-prefix guard in runs.py (e.g. dropping the startswith check) would send a non-prefix as cache_prefix and mis-split the system prompt at the runner, with no failing workflow-step test.
advisory.suggested_fix: Extend test_execution_mode.py with two cases using system_prompt=prefix+suffix: one where inputs['shared_prefix']==prefix (expect req.cache_prefix==prefix) and one where it is unrelated (expect None).

evidence: schema still requires plan: `"required": ["plan", "shared_prefix", "instructions", "input_too_large_ids"]` (plan_review_prerequisite_verify_inputs_output.schema.json:12)

advisory.finding: The prerequisite verify-inputs seam retains `plan` as a required output key that no consumer reads: the verifier template dropped `{{plan}}`, the gate YAML `prerequisite_verify` step's `with:` no longer passes `plan` (only `shared_prefix`/`instructions`/`input_too_large_ids`), yet `prerequisite_workflow_ops.plan_review_prerequisite_verify_inputs` still emits `plan` (line 129) and the schema still lists it in `required` (line 12). The sibling agentic seam (`plan_review_verify_inputs_output.schema.json`) made the parallel change cleanly — dropping `plan` to `{shared_prefix, instructions}` — so this variant is an asymmetric, dead-but-required contract key.
advisory.suggested_fix: Remove `plan` from `plan_review_prerequisite_verify_inputs_output.schema.json` (both `properties` and `required`), drop `"plan": subject_plan` from the op's return in prerequisite_workflow_ops.py, and update the assertion in test_plan_review_prerequisites_heldout.py — mirroring the `plan_review_verify_inputs` cleanup.
